title: Security review
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for authorized, local-only security review of code: scope check, threat model, a 16-area catalog, sandbox reproduction, tested fixes and independent review, with a worked example of the finding checks.
boundaries: Review only code the requester owns or is explicitly authorized to review, from a local copy. Never scan, probe, exploit or load-test any running system, including the requester's own production.
Findings go only to the requester. Disclosure to anyone else is the owner's separate decision.
Report where a secret is, never its value. Never try a found credential.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: Scope rules for security review
nouns.category_reason: A reusable set of guardrails every verb in this pack must follow.

rules: Review only code the requester owns or is explicitly authorized to review, from a local copy. Never scan, probe, exploit or load-test any running system, including the requester's own production.
Findings go only to the requester. Disclosure to anyone else is the owner's separate decision.
Report where a secret is, never its value. Never try a found credential.
The authorization noun names the requester, the target, the exact commit, the allowed activities and an expiry; an expired or missing authorization means blocked.
Sandboxes have no credentials and no network beyond local services the sandbox itself starts.
Never weaken a security control to make a reproduction or a test pass.

nouns.title: Security check catalog: 16 areas
nouns.category_reason: A fixed catalog of review areas that every review is measured against.

areas.asks: Every read or write of a private resource checks the caller's right to that exact resource on the server.
Credentials, tokens and sessions are created, stored, expired and revoked safely.
Untrusted input never reaches a SQL query, shell command, template or interpreter without parameterization or strict validation.
User-controlled paths cannot escape their intended directory.
User-controlled URLs cannot make the server reach internal or unintended destinations.
Untrusted bytes are never deserialized into executable objects.
Untrusted text is encoded for its output context, so it cannot run as script in a browser.
State-changing browser requests need proof they came from the site itself.
Secrets are not in code, logs, errors, client bundles or CI output.
Known advisories are checked against reachable code paths, with the tool and database date.
CI never runs untrusted code with secrets or write tokens, and third-party actions are pinned.
Passwords use a slow salted hash, randomness comes from a secure source and no custom cryptography is used.
Expensive operations have rate limits and quotas so one caller cannot exhaust capacity or budget.
Uploaded files have type, size and storage limits and are never executed or served unsafely.
Logs omit personal data and credentials, and log retention is bounded.
Model and tool outputs, retrieved documents and task text are treated as data: they cannot widen a tool's permissions, choose destinations or become commands without checks.

value.note: agent-tool-boundaries covers systems where models or agents call tools; skip it otherwise.

nouns.title: Severity rubric and deterministic finding checks
nouns.category_reason: A scoring rubric with deterministic checks and golden fixtures with recorded expected results.

severity_levels.critical: Remote, unauthenticated compromise of data or systems, or exposure of credentials with broad access.
severity_levels.high: Unauthorized access to other users' data or actions with modest preconditions.
severity_levels.medium: Limited impact, or significant preconditions such as an existing account with special rights.
severity_levels.low: Defense in depth: hard to exploit or small impact.
severity_levels.informational: A risky pattern with no demonstrated impact.

value.confidence_rule: High needs a local reproduction; reasoning from code alone is at most medium.

deterministic_checks.why: Reproductions target only local sandboxes: every host named must be localhost, a loopback address or .invalid.
Report where a secret is, never its value.

finding.title: Any signed-in user can read another user's invoice
finding.explanation: The handler loads the invoice by id and returns it without comparing its owner with the caller.
finding.reproduction: In a local sandbox build with two made-up users, user B requested user A's invoice at http://localhost:8000/invoices/1 and received it.
finding.fix: Compare invoice.owner_id with the caller's id before returning; add a test that user B is refused.

finding.title: Retrieved page text can choose the fetch tool's next destination
finding.explanation: The fetch tool follows a URL extracted from the previous page's text with no allowlist.
finding.reproduction: Not run: reasoning from code only. A local fixture page containing a link to http://127.0.0.1:9/ would show whether the tool follows it.
finding.fix: Restrict destinations to the task's declared allowlist and treat page text as data.

verbs.summary: Confirm the authorization covers this requester, target, commit and activities and has not expired, before any review work.

slots.description: Pin of the local snapshot to review, shaped like repo-review's snapshot template.

steps: Verify both pins.
Compare requester, target and commit between the authorization and the snapshot.

verbs.title: Propose a tested fix
verbs.summary: Write the smallest patch that fixes a confirmed finding plus a test that fails before and passes after, without pushing anything.
verbs.outcome: A fix noun pinned by patch digest, or no_change when the fix belongs to the owner's design decision.
steps: Write a test that fails on the pinned commit, then the smallest patch that makes it pass.
Run the existing test suite in the sandbox. Never weaken another control.
Store the patch by digest. Do not push, merge or open a pull request.

acceptance.check: The fix validates against template.fix's schema.
The added test failed before the patch and passed after it.
tests_passed is true from an actual sandbox run.

network: None beyond reading the local copy. No requests to any deployed system.

verbs.title: Independently review the findings
verbs.summary: A different worker reruns the rubric checks and decides whether each finding is upheld, downgraded or rejected.
steps: Confirm you wrote none of the findings; otherwise return blocked.
Rerun every deterministic check.
Downgrade confidence for findings without reproduction; reject findings that break the scope rules.
Findings go only to the requester. Disclosure to anyone else is the owner's separate decision.
